questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Other

questions.question: Please explain: *
questions.answer: Personal development, i think exchange widens my view on the world an gives one alot of life skills while getting to explore a new culture.

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Cost of living, courses i could get approved, new and interesting country/city to me

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: it was okay i would say, could be hard to find out who to contact when, in Prague there are a lot of different ERASMUS student groups and some work with the university some dont.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Intro days.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: The university offered student dorms, they are quite old and worn down. I was fine with it due to the affordable price, but it is definitely not for everyone, barely what you can call a kitchen (one stove top per floor, no eating area, small table, no chairs or shelves, need to have all you own cooking supplies) and shared bathrooms. you share a badly taken care of dorm room with one other person.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Its cheap and public transport is great so you can get around quite easily.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: had to go to the Erasmus office and fill in a few papers

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Erasmus club at my faculty and the Erasmus office

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: It was mostly my home university that made this difficult, host university were very easy to work with.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: quite an easy process, they are flexible and helpful, dont stress to much over it

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: Both

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: it is common for BA students in Prague to take MA level courses, so some courses are on MA level but available for BA.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Very different, at UCPH you study so you can pass an exam. AT CU you study out of curiosity and the syllabus is more flexible to accommodate student wishes and interests, a lot more presentations by students, guest lectures and in general teaching to learn more than teaching to pass an exam.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Fungal Pathogens and Interaction with their Hosts
Molecular Cloning
Plant, fungal and bacterial viruses
Parasitology
Developmental biology - a practical course
RNA structure and function
Plant Cytoskeleton
Model organisms in Developmental Biology
Modern methods in protein research
Toxicology
Animal models in immunology

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Listed are the courses i enjoyed the most, in general "intensive courses" are great fun, they are courses that take a full time for a week or so and are usually labs or field trips, great fun and where i learned the most.
Molecular Cloning
Plant, fungal and bacterial viruses
Parasitology
Developmental biology - a practical course
Toxicology
Animal models in immunology

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: i spent soo much more on exploring the country than i thought (in a good way, it is still cheap just did a lot more than i thought i would)

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: accommodation and student public transport card are so cheap.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: mostly activities run by the Erasmus club (run by local students) at the uni

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: science faculty Erasmus club

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Visit the other cities and the neighbouring countries as well as the nature and castles. Make sure to explore the city everyday, exchange goes by so fast so dont sleep on that, do something everyday.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: when you are well behaved its very easy, unfortunately a lot of tourists are vare poorly behaved so just dont act like them.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: go to the Erasmus club events, this is a club of local students that would love to get to know you!

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Not much, drinking culture is a lot more relaxed than in denmark, a beer or more like a coffee in denmark, its common to almost go out everyday but only for a single beer to talk with friends.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: its so normal to go out with friends in public, mostly due to it being so cheap to eat out or go for a drink.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Dont stress too much about course registration, you will figure it out when you arrive.
Be open and dont be afraid to say hi to new people, everyone feels that same as you do.
Go on the introduction ski trip/hut trip in the beginning of the exchange, one of the best experiences from my exchange.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: courses are valued between 1-5 ects, this is quite low compared to what im used to so you will have alot of courses

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: I have friends all over the world, got to know how universities are in other places and the life skills you gain form moving to another country.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Getting courses approved by UCPH, it seemed like the criteria are quite strict

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
